title: Stale reads caused by process pausing
body: In an Antithesis run against the main branch, one member's revision stopped progressing for a long time, but it continued accepting reads and writes. The resulting history has a linearizability failure. The cluster used ETCD_SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_ENTRIES=100, ETCD_SNAPSHOT_COUNT=50, and ETCD_COMPACTION_BATCH_LIMIT=10. I attached the Antithesis report, report dump, and a screenshot of the failure.

symptoms_visible: In the Antithesis history, one member's revision stops progressing for a long time while that member continues accepting reads and writes, and the history fails linearizability validation.
N0.label: N0 stale-member linearizability failure reported

symptoms_visible: The put of key26 with value 147 is reported at revision 3 by one client, while other clients observe that same put at revision 155.
N1.label: N1 conflicting revisions clarified

symptoms_visible: A transaction completed at proposed index 11 before a Range request began, but the Range request later received read index 10 and did not observe the completed write.
N2.label: N2 stale ReadIndex sequence established

symptoms_visible: The Antithesis run on the branch with the leadership-change select-race change still produced a linearizability failure.
N2_x.label: N2_x leadership-race candidate aftermath

symptoms_visible: During a long leader stall, the same read request ID is sent more than once; delayed messages are then processed after the cluster has advanced, and a later read is released with an older read index.
N3.label: N3 duplicate ReadIndex retry sequence captured

symptoms_visible: The unmodified debug build reproduced the linearizability failure in two of three runs, while four runs of the candidate build completed without detecting it.
N4.label: N4 candidate fix survives initial Antithesis runs

symptoms_visible: After the change landed, the periodic robustness tests completed five consecutive runs without reproducing the stale-read linearizability failure.
N_terminal.label: terminal periodic tests pass with landed fix

question_patterns: Can you describe the exact operation that violates linearizability?
What conflicting results do the clients observe in the history?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The put of key26 with value 147 gets revision 3 in client-4's watch and client-6's operation result, while the other clients' watch histories report that same put at revision 155.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clients all report the same revision; only their wall-clock timestamps differ.
The conflicting revisions are the same, but the key has a different generated name in another run.

question_patterns: Do the persisted database and WAL files show corruption or divergent data?
What did inspection of the report dump's DB and WAL files find?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I inspected the DB and WAL files and did not see a data problem, apart from a missing tombstone revision that was separately explained.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The members have irreconcilably different WAL entries for the same committed index.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c2. participant1 clarified the client-visible mismatch and inspected the artifacts; this affected-maintainer evidence is folded into the simulated user side rather than attributed to the opening reporter alone.

question_patterns: Can you instrument the transaction and Range paths and give the ordered timestamps around a failing read?
Does the stale read begin before or after the write completes in simulation time?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The transaction completed at 23.731 with revision 4 and proposed index 11. The Range request on another member started at 24.193, about 460 ms later, so the read began after the write completed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Range request started before the transaction completed, so the operations overlap.
The read started 500 ms after the write instead of 460 ms after it.

question_patterns: What commit, applied, and returned read-index values appear for the failing Range request?
Please capture the raw ReadIndex values associated with the completed write and stale read.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The write completed with proposed index 11, but the later Range request received ReadIndex 10 and therefore did not observe the write.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The later Range received read index 11 or higher and returned the newly written value.

question_patterns: What do the fault events in this Antithesis timeline actually do?
Can you clarify the pause, slowed partition, jam, and throttle events?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A node pause uses docker pause and later unpause; a slowed partition delays packets between the selected groups; a jam rate-limits one network link; and throttle reduces a container's CPU quota.

question_patterns: Can the cross-process timestamps and ordering in the Antithesis event log be trusted?
Are these timestamps generated from one deterministic simulation timeline?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, we can trust the time and order shown in the Antithesis logs.

edges.comment: Issue c8-c18 and c24. The reporter supplied debugger and request logs; participant2 clarified Antithesis fault semantics and ordering. Both contributors are folded into one technical user side.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as a race between the ReadIndex result and leadership-change notification, and change the select handling so a leadership change wins before the old result is accepted.
solution.concrete_example: Before accepting the ReadIndex result, check whether leadership changed and retry the read when it did.

edges.comment: Issue c19-c23 and c26. The reporter's initial select/leadership-race hypothesis was implemented, but one of three Antithesis runs reproduced the failure on that branch; the reporter explicitly withdrew this diagnosis.

question_patterns: Can you add tracing around ReadIndex requests, retries, and the read-only queue and share the raw sequence from a reproduction?
What request identifiers are sent before and after each timeout?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The follower sent read request ID 3744633826720154659, timed out, and retried twice using that exact same ID. It generated a different ID only after it noticed the leader change.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every retry already uses a fresh request ID, including retries to the same leader.
The same pattern occurs with different numeric request IDs in another run.

question_patterns: What messages arrive when the stalled member resumes?
Do any delayed responses for an earlier read remain in flight across the stall or leadership change?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the stalled member woke up, it processed delayed heartbeat responses carrying the old request ID after the cluster had advanced and another leader had been elected.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No delayed heartbeat response carries an earlier read request ID; all responses belong to the currently pending request.

question_patterns: What does the queue tracing show when the delayed retry is processed?
Please report the enqueue and dequeue order around the stale response.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The original request was dequeued, then a delayed retry with the same ID was received and queued again. A newer read was behind it, and processing the old delayed heartbeat sequence released the queued entries with the older cached index.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The queue trace never contains the same request ID again after it has been dequeued.

edges.comment: Issue c28-c43, especially c31 and the subsequent raft discussion. The answers preserve the reporter's logged identifiers and queue ordering; the general mechanism and remediation are scored on the final solution edge.

question_patterns: Can you run the candidate build for multiple long Antithesis simulations and compare it with the instrumented baseline?
Please test the candidate in several independent robustness runs and report only the pass or failure counts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The instrumented builds detected the issue in two of three runs. The candidate build detected it in zero of four runs, although I wanted to keep watching periodic tests before calling it fixed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate build reproduced the same stale-read failure in one of four runs.
The candidate passed five independent runs instead of four.

edges.comment: Issue c32-c34. These are pre-landing candidate-build measurements, so the edge changes knowledge rather than the persistent system state.

solution.intent: Prevent duplicate ReadIndex request contexts from entering raft during retries by generating a fresh read request ID for every retry, then verify the landed change with repeated periodic robustness runs.
solution.concrete_example: Change etcd's linearizable-read retry loop so each ReadIndex attempt receives a new request ID, even when retrying against the same leader. This prevents an old delayed request context from being inserted into the read-only queue again and later validating a newer read with a stale cached commit index. After landing, rerun the periodic Antithesis linearizability test repeatedly.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis combines the raw retry and queue trace with raft's readOnly semantics: reusing a RequestCtx allows a delayed duplicate to re-enter the queue, and an old quorum response can advance through that queue and release a newer request using a stale cached commit index. The reporter supplied the event sequence; connecting it to the queue contract is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Issue c42-c55. The maintainers accepted the etcd-side mitigation of never reusing the ReadIndex request context, landed it, and the reporter then observed repeated passing periodic runs. Release planning, cherry-pick coordination, and changelog work are intentionally omitted from scoring.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: etcd reused the same ReadIndex request context on timeout retries, allowing delayed duplicate traffic to re-enter raft's read-only queue and release a later read with a stale cached commit index.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the ordered evidence: a write at index 11 completed before the Range began, the Range received index 10, retries reused one request ID, and delayed heartbeat responses interacted with the queued requests.
The fix must generate a fresh ReadIndex request ID for every retry rather than reusing the prior request context.
Must not settle on the earlier leadership-change select-race hypothesis; a branch implementing that direction reproduced the linearizability failure.
Must ask for verification on a build containing the fix and must not declare resolution until repeated robustness runs no longer reproduce the failure.

persona_hint.experience_level: Expert etcd maintainer and robustness-test investigator; comfortable reading raft internals, adding Go instrumentation, using Delve, inspecting DB and WAL artifacts, and running long Antithesis simulations.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, highly technical, and evidence-driven; posts raw ordered logs and intermediate hypotheses, corrects timing mistakes openly, and withdraws hypotheses when new runs falsify them. Other affected maintainers and the Antithesis operator are folded into the same simulated user side where noted.
